en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Garlic Chapter.
5. The Training Rule on Purification by Water.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Nigrodha Monastery.
Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, she stood downwind, saying, "Blessed One, women have a foul odor.
Then the Blessed One—
“Let the bhikkhunīs take up the purification by water. Then the Blessed One instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī with a discourse on the Dhamma.

Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, having been instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a discourse on the Dhamma, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to her right, and departed.
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma concerning this cause and this occasion, addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow, monks, the water-cleansing for bhikkhunīs.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī,
thinking, “The Blessed One has allowed the water-cleansing,” began an excessively deep water-cleansing and caused a wound in her urinary tract.
Then that bhikkhunī informed the bhikkhunīs of this matter.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... [as before] ...were indignant, disparaged it, and complained, saying:
"How can a bhikkhunī undertake such an excessively deep water-cleansing ritual?"... [as before] ...
“Is it true, monks, that a bhikkhunī was practicing an excessively deep water-purification rite?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her... [as before]...
"How indeed, monks, could a bhikkhunī undertake a very deep water-cleansing?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of the faith of those who have it...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: ‘If a bhikkhunī undertakes a very deep water-cleansing, she commits an offense of wrong-doing.’"
“However, when a bhikkhunī takes up water for cleansing, she should take no more than two finger-joints’ depth. For one who exceeds that, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Cleansing with water is said to be the washing of the urinary organ.
"Taking up" means while washing.
"It should be taken up with no more than two finger-joints" means: [as follows].
Two joints at most may be taken from two fingers.
"Exceeding that" means:
if she consents to the contact, she exceeds it by even as much as a hair's breadth, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one takes [a toothpick] that exceeds two finger-breadths while perceiving it as exceeding [that length], there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one takes [a toothpick] that exceeds two finger-breadths while being in doubt, there is an offense of expiation.
If one takes [a toothpick] that exceeds two finger-breadths while perceiving it as less than that, there is an offense of expiation.
If the joint is less than two finger-breadths and one perceives it as more, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If the joint is less than two finger-breadths and one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If the joint is less than two finger-breadths and one perceives it as less, there is no offense.
There is no offense if one takes [the hair] up to the length of two finger-joints,
or if one takes it less than the length of two finger-joints.
On account of illness,
for one who is insane,
or for one who is a first-time offender.
The fifth training rule is concluded.
